turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
First, I will do one and explain my thinking.
"They sing at parties." I change "they" to "he". One person, so the verb gets -s: "He sings at parties."
Rule: after he, she or it, the verb takes -s or -es.
Right: My cat sleeps all day. Wrong: My cat sleep all day.

Now you. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
